name: University of Sussex

settingEvidence.evidence: Living on our beautiful green campus - the only university in a national park - you'll be just a few minutes' walk away from the library, lecture theatres, shops, cafés and bars.

contextual.summary: Applicants who meet any one of Sussex's contextual criteria are made a lower contextual offer, typically BCC at A-level for first-year degrees (about 25% of Sussex's UK conditional offers are contextual).
contextual.typicalReduction: Typical contextual offer for first-year degrees: BCC for A-levels (DMM for a BTEC Extended Diploma). The exact reduction in grades varies depending on the course.

criteria.detail: Your home postcode on the UCAS application is in decile 1 or 2 of the Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD); Sussex makes the offer automatically.
Your home postcode on the UCAS application is in POLAR4 quintile 1; Sussex makes the offer automatically.
You received free school meals while attending secondary school. Sussex uses the free school meals information on your UCAS application (students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland).
You have been looked after in care for more than three months; tick the care-experienced box on the UCAS form.
You are an estranged student (studying without the support and approval of a family network); tell the admissions team when you apply.
You have refugee status or Humanitarian Protection; use the residential category on the UCAS form to show this.
You are a young carer (under 18, helping to look after a family member who is ill, disabled, has a mental health condition or misuses drugs or alcohol); tell the admissions team when you apply.
You are registered on the Sussex Inspires programme (Year 12) and meet Sussex's widening participation criteria; Sussex applies the contextual offer to all registered students who do.

You are a student at a partner college with a Progression Agreement (East Sussex College Group, Varndean College, Littlehampton Academy, Brighton Aldridge Community Academy, Thomas Bennett Community College); the contextual offer is automatic.

Sussex says it will still consider you for a contextual offer if you have faced other challenges that disrupted your education (for example disability, serious bereavement, long-term illness or homelessness).

contextual.rulesText: You will qualify if you meet any of the criteria listed. Postcode (IMD or POLAR4) and free school meals are picked up automatically from your UCAS application; for care, estranged and young carer status you are encouraged to tell Sussex's admissions team. The exact reduction in grades varies depending on the course.

programmes.name: Sussex Inspires
programmes.summary: A free Year 12 programme of university visits, taster sessions, UCAS and student finance support and a July 2027 summer school, with a contextual offer if you also meet Sussex's widening participation criteria.
programmes.whoCanApply: Students in Year 12 of college or sixth form (or year 1 of college) studying A-levels, BTECs, a T-Level or another Level 3. Anyone in the UK can apply, but places are limited and Sussex gives priority to widening participation students.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Anyone in the UK can apply. Places are limited, so priority goes to students who: get the 16-19 bursary; had free school meals or pupil premium at secondary school; have lived in care; are from a Gypsy, Roma or Traveller background; live in an area where fewer young people go to university; are estranged from their parents or guardians; are young carers; or are refugees or asylum seekers. To complete the programme you attend at least three of the four main events. Some events start at 10am and Sussex can only provide train tickets from London to the Falmer campus.
benefits: Free; travel costs covered (train or bus ticket emailed before each event, but train tickets only from London to Falmer)
Taster sessions, subject days and a Find your Future workshop on UCAS applications and student finance
Priority access to Sussex's summer school in July 2027 if you complete the programme

Economics is taught in the University of Sussex Business School. Sussex offers two main degrees: Economics BA (lighter on maths and statistics) and Economics BSc (more quantitative); neither page lists required A-level subjects, but GCSE Maths grade 6 is required (grade 5 considered with some A-levels, including Maths and Psychology).
